proposals: PPAC should publish refinery-wise annual hydrogen consumption, split by source — steam methane reforming, electrolysis and other — with hydrogen used per barrel of diesel hydrotreated, so cost estimates no longer rest on a US industry figure of 200 standard cubic feet per barrel.

The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy should publish the discovered price for each of the four SIGHT Mode-2B refinery awards, not only IOCL's ₹397 a kilogram, so the green-hydrogen premium faced by Numaligarh, Bina and Vizag can be compared on the same basis.

The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy should publish a quarterly status report for each SIGHT refinery award, giving construction milestones, commissioning date and tonnes of green hydrogen actually delivered, so progress on Panipat's December 2027 target and the 30 KTPA total is checkable.

PPAC should publish an annual estimate, from refiners' own data, of the hydrogen cost embedded in a litre of diesel, separating grey and green supply, so this piece's worked estimate of a ₹0.55–0.80 a litre premium for full substitution can be tested against official numbers.
